$comment: The one component map. typescript/scripts/ci-scope.mjs reads it to decide which CI consumers a changed path selects; release-cut.mjs reads it for released-root membership at the exact main cut.
components: who owns which paths. `owns` roots minus `excludes` decide ownership, a `selectedBy` glob wins over the root, and `package` is the Cargo package.

rules: ordered, the first rule whose `paths` match a changed path decides native verification (Rust, tooling and E2E jobs). No match retains full native verification. Component ownership and Office-specific machinery decide frozen Office verification in ci-scope.mjs; rules do not select Office.

Office SPA, browser and local-service/companion verification share the ownership-only Office selector in ci-scope.mjs; weekly/manual runs cover shared inputs, while merge groups and main pushes never select Office work.

migrations: the source files that list a component's SQLite migrations; outside the alpha channel a release that has more entries in one than the last published release of that component is held for the owner, while an alpha only reports them (typescript/scripts/publication-gates.mjs).

skills: true when the component's native archive carries the agent-skills tree extensions/<name>/skills (cargo-dist include ../../skills); typescript/scripts/component-skills.mjs reads it for the archive policy and verifier, and component-skills.test.ts checks the tree and the include.
scopedChecks: a component that cannot affect the others (only Squad) lists the native test files and E2E files its own scope runs; ci-scope.mjs turns that into the native_scope outputs.

Globs: `**` matches any path, `*` and `?` stay inside one directory. A rule may only narrow selection for a path that provably no job of the dropped consumer reads; ci-scope.test.ts guards each narrowed class.

releaseConsumers: a private leaf adds its owned changes to named packaged products, including products awaiting activation, without replacing matching released-root membership; ownership, CI scope and version updates remain independent.

A private component may declare release:false, with or without a Cargo package; it owns files but gets no release. Binary targets require explicit package.metadata.dist.dist=false; library-only crates need no opt-out. A crate that inherits the workspace version keeps its Cargo.lock entry in the release of the component that owns rust/Cargo.toml, whoever owns the crate.

releaseStatus: only with release:false; never means no released product contains this leaf and forbids releaseConsumers, parked means explicitly deferred publication. Absence means awaiting activation. This does not change CI selection.
initialVersion: owner-approved first alpha seed; requiresCliSha: supporting CLI registration commit that must be in its newest published release before a first product cut.
bootstrapSha: first-release history boundary for the release cut (#1399); the last commit before the component existed, kept unchanged.

neverShippedPaths.reason: Repository development references, outside the canonical CLI and product skill bundles.
Cargo integration tests and fixtures, outside canonical release inputs.

testOnlyReferences.reason: The parent declares this fixture helper immediately after #[cfg(test)].

generatedInputs.reason: The canonical release script builds the app and pins this directory before Cargo generates immutable asset snapshots.

rules.why: The private presentation leaf retains conservative full native verification. Colab guidance and Remote pages embed the checked CSS; Office web jobs do not consume this isolated leaf.

Shared tokens project checked CSS embedded by native Colab guidance and Remote pages, and are read by Rust CLI palette and contrast tests; Site has its own workflow watching this path. Office web checks read none of these files.
Native Colab embeds these app stylesheets in its public guidance asset, so CSS-only changes require Rust compilation and socket tests.
Read by build and test inputs: design/cli-style.md by the CLI and Squad style tests, rust/archive/NATIVE-INSTALL.md by the release archive and onboarding checks.
Prose read only by the formatter in Code quality, which always runs; no test or build input reads it (guarded by ci-scope.test.ts).
The handbook website has its own workflow (.github/workflows/site.yml); no native or Office job reads it.

Private MV3 shell has its own browser-addon.yml workflow filtered to shell and consumed tooling inputs; native and Office jobs read none of its files. Positive and prefix-negative fixtures guard this boundary.
Colab Rust retains full workspace checks; frozen Office selection follows its own ownership rather than private release ownership.
Remote Rust retains full workspace checks; frozen Office selection follows its own ownership rather than private release ownership.
The Office application and its documentation: checked by the Office web jobs only.
Rust workspace, embedded skills and the Squad extension: checked by the native jobs; the Office web checks read none of it.
Office's Rust crates remain in workspace Cargo checks and select the frozen Office web, local-service and companion suites through Office ownership.
Test suites and E2E scenarios retain native coverage. Office-owned native suites additionally select Office verification; shared support changes rely on weekly/manual Office runs.
